data.name: read
data.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

promptGuidelines: Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.

data.name: bash
data.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

promptGuidelines: You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.

data.name: powershell
data.description: Execute a PowerShell command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

promptGuidelines: You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.

data.name: edit
data.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

promptGuidelines: Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.

data.name: write
data.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

promptGuidelines: Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.

data.name: grep
data.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

data.name: find
data.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

data.name: ls
data.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

data.name: ask_user
data.description: Post a set of questions to the user in an interactive form and end this run. Answers arrive later as a follow-up message; the user may leave any question unanswered.

id.description: Unique within this call; used as the answer key reported back to you.

question.description: The question itself, as one plain-text line.

detail.description: Optional supporting context shown under the question.

value.description: Stable machine value reported back to you when the user picks this option.

label.description: Short label the user reads, ideally a few words.

detail.description: Optional clarification shown under the label.

options.description: Options to choose from. Omit when free text is the whole answer; the interface always offers a Custom answer.

multiple.description: Allow several options at once. Default: one answer per question.

questions.description: The questions to post, in the order the user should read them. Every question may be left unanswered.

promptGuidelines: When you cannot continue the requested work without a missing fact, scope choice, or decision from the user, and ask_user is available, use it instead of ending with a prose question. Group related questions in one call. Do not use it for ordinary conversation, rhetorical questions, or optional follow-up suggestions; if the tool is unavailable, ask in prose. An answer to ask_user is clarification, not authorization for a sensitive action. The tool ends the run; answers, including unanswered questions, arrive as a follow-up message that wakes you. Call it alone and last, and do not repost the same questions or poll for answers.
